pain-injury-recovery.title: Pain & Injury Recovery
pain-injury-recovery.tagline: Restoring function and reducing pain through targeted needle therapy
overview: Whether you're dealing with chronic pain, a recent injury, muscle tension, headaches, or restricted movement, acupuncture offers a comprehensive approach to supporting recovery and helping you return to the activities you enjoy.

Acupuncture has been shown to influence several systems involved in pain and healing. Research suggests it may help regulate the nervous system, stimulate the release of the body's natural pain-relieving chemicals, improve circulation, and reduce muscle tension. By addressing both the source of discomfort and the body's response to pain, treatment can help promote lasting improvements rather than simply masking symptoms.

At Five Points Wellness, treatments are tailored to your individual needs and may incorporate a variety of techniques, including traditional acupuncture, trigger point therapy, motor point acupuncture, cupping, gua sha, and other supportive therapies when appropriate.
addresses: Low back, neck, and shoulder pain

sections.title: Musculoskeletal Pain
sections.description: Acupuncture and orthopedic needling are highly effective for joint and soft tissue pain throughout the body. Treatment targets the specific muscles, tendons, and fascial structures involved — reducing inflammation, releasing trigger points, and restoring normal movement patterns.

sections.title: Headaches
sections.description: Acupuncture has strong clinical evidence for headache reduction — both in frequency and intensity. Treatment addresses the underlying drivers, whether vascular, muscular, or stress-related, rather than simply suppressing the symptom.

pain-injury-recovery.howItHelps: Acupuncture reduces inflammation, promotes tissue repair, and interrupts pain signaling pathways — providing relief that compounds over a course of treatment. Orthopedic needling techniques targeting motor points and trigger points are often combined with traditional acupuncture for musculoskeletal presentations.
pain-injury-recovery.whatToExpect: Initial sessions focus on reducing acute pain and inflammation. As treatment progresses, sessions shift toward restoring range of motion, strengthening the body's natural repair mechanisms, and preventing recurrence. Most patients notice meaningful improvement within 4–6 sessions.

stress-sleep-wellness.title: Stress, Sleep & General Wellness
stress-sleep-wellness.tagline: Calming the nervous system and supporting the body's innate capacity to restore itself
overview: Stress, poor sleep, and chronic fatigue often reflect a nervous system that is stuck in a heightened state of activation. Over time, this can affect mood, energy, digestion, immunity, and overall well-being.
Acupuncture offers a structured way to help regulate the nervous system, supporting the body's ability to shift out of "fight or flight" and into a more restorative state.
At Five Points Wellness, treatments are individualized to help restore balance in both the body and mind.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Stress & Nervous System Regulation
paragraphs: Modern research suggests acupuncture may influence several key systems involved in stress regulation:
items: The autonomic nervous system (fight or flight / rest and digest balance)
Neurotransmitters involved in mood and relaxation
Muscle tension patterns related to chronic stress

sections.title: Sleep Support & Insomnia
sections.description: Sleep disturbances are often connected to both physical and emotional stress patterns. When the nervous system remains overactive, it can become difficult to fall asleep, stay asleep, or reach restorative sleep stages. Many patients report improved sleep quality, deeper rest, and easier sleep onset over a series of treatments.

sections.title: Fatigue & Low Energy
sections.description: Ongoing stress can lead to both mental and physical fatigue. This is often related to prolonged nervous system activation, poor sleep quality, and muscular tension. Rather than simply stimulating energy, treatment focuses on restoring balance so that energy levels regulate more naturally over time.

sections.title: What Treatment Feels Like
sections.description: Acupuncture for stress and sleep is typically very calming. Thin sterile needles are placed in specific points chosen based on your symptoms, stress patterns, sleep quality, and overall constitution. Treatments are gentle and fully customized to your comfort level.
items: A sense of heaviness or restfulness
In some cases, falling asleep during treatment

stress-sleep-wellness.howItHelps: Because the nervous system influences nearly every function in the body, stress and sleep issues are often connected to other symptoms such as digestive irregularity, headaches, muscle tightness, hormonal fluctuations, and difficulty recovering from exercise or injury. For this reason, treatment is often designed to support overall regulation rather than focusing on a single symptom in isolation.
stress-sleep-wellness.whatToExpect: Many patients notice improved relaxation after the first session, with better sleep quality often emerging within several treatments. Reduced stress reactivity, more stable energy levels, and an improved sense of emotional balance tend to develop over a series of visits. Chronic stress patterns typically require consistent treatment for longer-lasting changes in the nervous system.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help anxiety or stress?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is commonly used to support the body's stress response and promote a calmer nervous system state.

faqs.q: How quickly will I notice changes in sleep?
faqs.a: Some patients notice improvement within a few sessions, while others experience gradual changes over time.

faqs.q: Will I fall asleep during treatment?
faqs.a: Many patients do. This is a common sign of deep relaxation.

faqs.q: How often should I come in?
faqs.a: Frequency depends on symptom severity, but many patients begin with weekly treatments and adjust based on response.

womens-health-fertility.title: Women's Health & Fertility
womens-health-fertility.tagline: Supporting hormonal balance, reproductive health, and the full arc of women's wellness
overview: Women's health concerns often involve complex interactions between hormones, stress, sleep, digestion, and nervous system regulation. Acupuncture offers a supportive, individualized approach that works alongside both natural cycles and conventional medical care.
At Five Points Wellness, treatments are designed to support reproductive health, hormonal balance, and overall well-being at every stage of life.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Women's Health
paragraphs: Acupuncture is commonly used to help regulate systems involved in hormonal and reproductive function. Research suggests it may influence:

addresses: Mood changes related to the menstrual cycle
Fertility support — IVF and IUI adjunct

sections.title: Fertility Support
sections.description: Acupuncture is commonly used to support fertility at multiple stages of the reproductive journey, including natural conception and assisted reproductive treatments such as IVF and IUI. Each treatment plan is individualized based on cycle phase, health history, and current fertility plan.
items: Improving blood flow to the uterus and ovaries

sections.title: IVF & Assisted Reproductive Support
sections.description: For patients undergoing IVF or other assisted reproductive technologies, acupuncture is often used as supportive care throughout different stages of the process. Care is tailored based on where you are in your treatment cycle and coordinated to complement your medical care when appropriate.
items: Supporting relaxation and nervous system regulation

sections.title: Fertility is a Two-Partner Process
paragraphs: In cases of infertility or difficulty conceiving, it is important to recognize that fertility involves both partners. For this reason, a semen analysis is often recommended as part of a comprehensive fertility evaluation, in addition to assessment of ovulation, hormone levels, and reproductive health in the female partner.
Male factor fertility issues are more common than many people realize and can contribute to difficulty conceiving even when the female partner's cycles appear normal.

Regardless of the results of fertility testing, it is often beneficial for both partners to receive supportive care. Acupuncture may help support overall reproductive health by addressing factors such as stress regulation, circulation, sleep quality, and hormonal balance in both individuals.
A collaborative approach between partners and healthcare providers often provides the most complete picture and the best support for reproductive health and conception goals.

sections.title: Stress, Sleep & Reproductive Health
sections.description: Stress and reproductive health are closely connected. Elevated or chronic stress can influence hormonal signaling, ovulation, cycle regularity, and overall reproductive function. Many treatment plans integrate both fertility-focused and stress-focused acupuncture strategies.

womens-health-fertility.howItHelps: Because these systems are interconnected, treatment is always individualized based on your specific symptoms and goals. Rather than targeting a single symptom, treatment focuses on overall regulatory balance across hormonal and nervous system function.
womens-health-fertility.whatToExpect: Response varies depending on individual health history and goals, but patients often report improved cycle awareness and regularity, reduced PMS symptoms, improved stress resilience, and better sleep and energy balance. Fertility and hormonal health often require a consistent treatment approach over time for best results.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help fertility?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is commonly used as supportive care for fertility by helping regulate stress, circulation, and reproductive function.

faqs.q: Can I do acupuncture while undergoing IVF?
faqs.a: Yes. Many patients use acupuncture alongside IVF or IUI as supportive care throughout their treatment cycle.

faqs.q: How often should I come in?
faqs.a: Frequency depends on your goals. Many patients begin with weekly treatments, with adjustments based on cycle timing or treatment phase.

faqs.q: Does acupuncture regulate periods?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is often used to support cycle regularity by influencing hormonal and nervous system balance.

digestive-support.title: Digestive Support
digestive-support.tagline: IBS, Bloating, Constipation & Gut Health Support
overview: Digestive health issues such as bloating, constipation, diarrhea, acid reflux, and IBS are often linked to imbalances in the gut–brain axis, stress response, and nervous system regulation.
Acupuncture is commonly used as a natural, holistic approach for digestive issues, supporting both digestive function and the body's ability to regulate stress-related gut symptoms.
At Five Points Wellness, treatment is customized to support digestive health, gut motility, and abdominal comfort while addressing underlying contributing factors.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Digestive Health
paragraphs: Research suggests acupuncture may help influence:
items: IBS symptoms (IBS-C, IBS-D, and mixed IBS)
Vagal nerve activity and "rest and digest" function

sections.title: IBS, Bloating & Constipation Support
sections.description: Many patients seek acupuncture for support with common digestive complaints that may not fully respond to diet changes or medication alone.

sections.title: Gut–Brain Axis & Stress
sections.description: The gut–brain connection plays a major role in digestive health. Stress, anxiety, and chronic nervous system activation can directly affect digestion. Acupuncture is often used for stress-related digestive issues, helping shift the body out of a heightened stress response and into a more regulated "rest and digest" state.

sections.title: What Treatment Feels Like
sections.description: Acupuncture for digestive health is typically calming and restorative. Fine sterile needles are selected based on your specific symptoms, digestion patterns, and overall health presentation.
items: A sense of digestive ease or movement

digestive-support.howItHelps: By supporting the nervous system and digestive signaling pathways, acupuncture may help restore more balanced and comfortable digestion. Treatment addresses both the digestive system directly and the stress and nervous system patterns that contribute to gut dysfunction.
digestive-support.whatToExpect: Results vary depending on severity and duration of symptoms, but many patients report reduced bloating and abdominal discomfort, more regular bowel movements, improved digestion after meals, less stress-related gut flare-ups, and better energy and overall gut stability. Chronic digestive conditions often improve gradually with consistent treatment and nervous system regulation.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help IBS?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture is commonly used to support IBS symptoms by helping regulate gut motility, stress response, and nervous system balance.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help bloating?
faqs.a: Many patients report reduced bloating and improved digestion as the gut begins to regulate.

faqs.q: How many sessions do I need?
faqs.a: Some people notice changes within a few sessions, while chronic digestive issues may require ongoing treatment.

faqs.q: Does stress affect digestion?
faqs.a: Yes. Stress is one of the most common contributors to digestive dysfunction due to its impact on the gut–brain axis.

immune-autoimmune.title: Immune System & Autoimmune Conditions
immune-autoimmune.tagline: Modulating immune function and reducing the inflammatory burden of chronic disease
overview: Acupuncture exerts measurable effects on immune cell activity, cytokine production, and systemic inflammation — making it a valuable adjunct for both under-active and overactive immune presentations. Autoimmune and chronic inflammatory conditions occur when the immune system becomes dysregulated, leading to symptoms such as fatigue, pain, inflammation, and fluctuating systemic function.

At Five Points Wellness, treatment is adapted to your current symptom presentation, with an emphasis on improving resilience, reducing flare intensity, and supporting long-term regulation. It is used as a complementary therapy alongside medical care and is not a replacement for ongoing treatment with your healthcare provider.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Immune Function
paragraphs: Research demonstrates acupuncture's ability to regulate T-cell populations, reduce pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-6, and enhance natural killer cell activity. These effects on immune cell activity and cytokine production make acupuncture a meaningful adjunct for managing both the inflammatory burden of overactive immune conditions and the vulnerability of underactive immune presentations.

Because immune and nervous system function are closely interconnected, treatment is designed to support overall system regulation rather than targeting isolated symptoms alone. Research suggests acupuncture may help modulate immune signaling pathways, regulate inflammatory cytokine production, balance sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system activity, support stress response and cortisol regulation, and improve circulation and tissue oxygenation.

sections.title: Kiiko Matsumoto Approach to Autoimmune Conditions
paragraphs: Treatment at Five Points Wellness incorporates principles from the Kiiko Matsumoto style of acupuncture — a Japanese clinical approach that emphasizes abdominal diagnosis, palpation-based assessment, and functional pattern identification. This method uses physical palpation of the abdomen and meridian system to identify areas of imbalance and guide treatment in real time.

Treatment is based on abdominal and meridian palpation findings, functional pattern assessment rather than symptom isolation, and gentle stimulation of key regulatory acupuncture points that support organ system communication and nervous system regulation. This approach allows treatment to be highly individualized and responsive to changes in symptom presentation, which is especially important in fluctuating chronic inflammatory conditions.

sections.title: Flare Management & Treatment Frequency
paragraphs: During periods of symptom flare, acupuncture is often used more intensively to help regulate the system and reduce symptom duration. Treatment once or twice per week during an active flare may be recommended depending on severity and individual response. The goals during flare support are to reduce symptom intensity, shorten flare duration, calm nervous system overactivation, and support a faster return to baseline function.

As symptoms stabilize, treatment frequency is typically reduced to maintenance care — weekly, biweekly, or monthly sessions depending on individual needs — to sustain gains and reduce flare frequency over the long term.

sections.title: Immune Resilience & Prevention
paragraphs: Acupuncture is also commonly used to support immune system resilience and prevention of recurrent illness, particularly for individuals who experience frequent colds, seasonal susceptibility, or slow recovery from sickness. By supporting regulatory systems, acupuncture may help the body respond to stressors more efficiently and recover more quickly.

Stress is a major contributor to immune dysfunction — and because the nervous system and immune system are so tightly linked, supporting one invariably supports the other. Treatment may also benefit sleep quality, respiratory and sinus health, and overall energy and vitality.

sections.title: A Whole-Body Approach to Immune Health
paragraphs: Immune function is influenced by multiple interconnected systems including stress and emotional regulation, sleep quality, digestive and gut health, hormonal balance, and environmental and inflammatory triggers. For this reason, treatment is designed to support overall system balance rather than focusing on a single isolated symptom.

Many patients seek acupuncture support for chronic fatigue, joint and muscle pain, inflammatory flare-ups, stress-related symptom aggravation, and low resilience or slow recovery from illness. Treatment plans are regularly adjusted based on current presentation and response.

immune-autoimmune.howItHelps: For autoimmune patients, acupuncture's regulation of T-cell populations and reduction of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-6 translates to reduced joint pain and inflammation, improved fatigue levels, and better management of flare cycles. Natural killer cell activity is also enhanced, supporting more robust immune surveillance without the broad suppression associated with pharmacological immune modulation.
immune-autoimmune.whatToExpect: Response to treatment is typically gradual and cumulative. Patients often report reduced stress and nervous system activation, improved energy regulation, decreased pain or inflammatory discomfort, improved sleep quality, and reduced severity and frequency of flare-ups over time. Because autoimmune conditions are chronic and complex, treatment takes a longer-term perspective and plans are adjusted frequently as symptoms evolve.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help autoimmune conditions?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is not a cure, but it is commonly used as a supportive therapy to help regulate inflammation, stress response, and symptom burden. It works best alongside — not instead of — your existing medical care.

faqs.q: How often should I come in during a flare?
faqs.a: During active flare-ups, many patients benefit from treatment 1–2 times per week depending on symptom severity and individual response. Frequency is reduced to maintenance care as symptoms stabilize.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help prevent illness?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is often used to support immune resilience, reduce stress-related immune suppression, and improve recovery from illness — particularly for patients with frequent colds or seasonal susceptibility.

faqs.q: Is acupuncture safe for autoimmune conditions?
faqs.a: Yes. When performed by a licensed practitioner, acupuncture is generally safe and commonly used alongside medical care. Treatment is adapted to your current presentation and always coordinated with your existing providers.

neurological-health.title: Neurological Health
neurological-health.tagline: Support for Nerve Pain, Migraines, Neuropathy & Nervous System Recovery
overview: Neurological conditions often involve complex interactions between the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and the autonomic nervous system. Symptoms such as pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, or muscle weakness can significantly impact daily function and quality of life.

Acupuncture offers an evidence-informed approach that supports nervous system regulation, nerve signaling, and neurological recovery. It is increasingly used as a complementary therapy alongside conventional neurological care.

At Five Points Wellness, treatment is tailored to the severity, chronicity, and presentation of each neurological condition, with a focus on supporting the body's natural healing and regulatory processes.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Neurological Function
paragraphs: Acupuncture has documented effects on both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Research suggests it may help:
items: Modulate pain signaling pathways in the brain and spinal cord
Influence neuroplasticity (the nervous system's ability to adapt and reorganize)

introSections.title: Scalp Acupuncture for Neurological Recovery
paragraphs: Scalp acupuncture is a specialized technique that involves needling specific zones on the scalp that correspond to functional areas of the brain. These regions are mapped to areas of the central nervous system associated with movement, sensation, coordination, and other neurological functions.

Because the scalp lies directly over the cerebral cortex, stimulation of these zones is used to influence neurological signaling and support functional recovery. This approach is commonly used in neurological and rehabilitative care, including post-stroke recovery, motor weakness, and sensory dysfunction.
In clinical practice, scalp acupuncture may be combined with traditional body acupuncture to support:
items: Neurological rehabilitation after injury or stroke

sections.title: How Acupuncture Helps Neurological Conditions
sections.description: Needle stimulation activates the body's natural neurochemical and pain-modulating systems. This may help:
items: Support nerve repair and regeneration in peripheral nerve injury
Improve circulation to affected neural tissues
Reduce muscle tension related to neurological dysfunction
Support sensory and motor function in affected areas

sections.title: Neurological Acupuncture & Whole-Body Health
sections.description: Neurological conditions are often interconnected with other systems in the body. Because of this, treatment may also support overall nervous system regulation rather than focusing solely on isolated symptoms.

neurological-health.howItHelps: Acupuncture is increasingly used as a supportive therapy in neurological rehabilitation and chronic nerve-related conditions. Treatment is always individualized based on your specific neurological presentation and medical history, and is designed to complement, not replace, existing medical management.
neurological-health.whatToExpect: Neurological recovery is typically gradual and varies based on the condition, severity, and duration of symptoms. Bell's palsy often shows measurable improvement within 6–10 sessions. Peripheral neuropathy may require ongoing or maintenance care for symptom management. Chronic neurological conditions improve gradually over time with consistent treatment. Progress is monitored at each visit and treatment is adjusted accordingly.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help nerve pain or neuropathy?
faqs.a: Acupuncture is commonly used to support symptoms of peripheral neuropathy, including numbness, tingling, and nerve-related pain.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help migraines?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture is frequently used to support migraine frequency, intensity, and tension-related headaches.

faqs.q: How long does neurological treatment take?
faqs.a: It depends on the condition. Some acute conditions like Bell's palsy may respond within several weeks, while chronic conditions often require longer-term care.

faqs.q: Is acupuncture safe for neurological conditions?
faqs.a: When performed by a licensed practitioner, acupuncture is generally considered safe and is often used as a complementary therapy alongside medical care.

sports-performance-recovery.title: Sports Performance & Recovery
sports-performance-recovery.tagline: Supporting athletes at every level — injury recovery, faster turnaround, and peak performance
overview: Athletes at every level use acupuncture to address acute injuries, accelerate recovery between training cycles, and maintain the structural and physiological conditions needed for sustained performance. Treatment integrates traditional acupuncture with orthopedic needling and motor point techniques specifically suited to the demands of athletic presentations.

Whether you are managing an overuse injury, preparing for a race, or looking to recover more efficiently between sessions, acupuncture is a versatile, drug-free tool that supports your body's ability to train harder, bounce back faster, and stay in the game longer.

introSections.title: How Acupuncture Supports Athletic Performance & Recovery
paragraphs: Acupuncture reduces local inflammation, promotes blood flow to injured and overworked tissue, releases myofascial trigger points, and restores normal muscle activation patterns. Motor point needling directly addresses neuromuscular dysfunction — a common driver of reduced strength, coordination, and movement quality in athletic injuries and overuse conditions.

Beyond injury treatment, acupuncture supports the nervous system's ability to regulate, which directly influences recovery rate, sleep quality, stress hormone balance, and how efficiently the body repairs tissue between training sessions. For athletes in high-volume training phases, this systemic regulation can be as valuable as the local injury work.

introSections.title: Pre- & Post-Event Support
paragraphs: Acupuncture can be used strategically around competition and training events. Pre-event treatment focuses on optimizing circulation, regulating the nervous system, reducing residual tension, and preparing the body to perform at its best. Post-event treatment shifts to accelerating tissue recovery, reducing inflammation, clearing metabolic waste, and supporting overall system reset.

Many athletes incorporate regular sessions during their competitive season for ongoing recovery support and injury prevention — moving away from a reactive model and toward proactive maintenance of the physical conditions that performance depends on.

addresses: IT band syndrome and runner's knee
Rotator cuff injuries and shoulder impingement
Low back pain and sacroiliac dysfunction
Recovery between training cycles and events

sections.title: Motor Point Needling for Athletes
paragraphs: Motor point acupuncture targets specific anatomical locations where the motor nerve enters the muscle belly. Because these points govern muscle activation, stimulating them can release chronic tension throughout the entire muscle, restore normal firing patterns, and improve both strength and coordination — often in a single session.

This approach is particularly effective for athletes dealing with muscle inhibition after injury, movement compensations that develop over a training season, and overuse patterns that accumulate over time. It works directly with the neuromuscular system to address the root cause of dysfunction rather than just the site of pain.

sections.title: Race Day & Event Package — Run Strong. Recover Faster.
paragraphs: Preparing for a race, triathlon, or other sporting event? Support your body before, during, and after your event with a targeted 3-session acupuncture package designed for athletes. Whether you're running your first 10K or lining up for a marathon, this protocol is built around your event timeline.

Session 1 — Pre-Race Performance Treatment (7–14 days before your event): Full acupuncture session focused on improving strength, endurance, and mobility; addressing any lingering injuries; and optional cupping for muscle recovery going into race week.

Session 2 — Nervous System Reset (1–3 days before your event): 30-minute ear acupuncture session only — no body needling, no risk of muscle soreness. This session is focused on reducing pre-race anxiety and optimizing focus and performance for race day.
Session 3 — Post-Race Recovery Session (1–7 days after your event): Full recovery session to decrease soreness and inflammation, support muscle recovery, and treat any race-related injuries.

Package pricing: $325 (a $408 value). Because sessions need to be scheduled around your specific event date, this package is booked by phone or text only — call or text (610) 742-5810 to coordinate your timeline. Book early to reserve your sessions, especially for local events where spots fill quickly.

sections.title: Ongoing Maintenance for Active Athletes
paragraphs: Athletes who incorporate regular acupuncture into their training routine — rather than only seeking treatment after injury — consistently report faster recovery, improved sleep, reduced muscle soreness, and greater training consistency over time. Regular sessions help the body stay ahead of the cumulative strain that builds across a training season.

Frequency depends on training volume, competition schedule, and individual needs. Many athletes benefit from weekly sessions during high-volume phases, transitioning to biweekly or monthly maintenance during off-season or reduced training periods.

sports-performance-recovery.howItHelps: Acupuncture reduces local inflammation, promotes blood flow to injured and overworked tissue, and releases myofascial trigger points through motor point needling. It restores normal muscle activation patterns that are disrupted by injury and overuse, and supports the nervous system regulation that governs sleep quality, stress hormone balance, and tissue repair rate. For athletes, this combination of local and systemic support creates conditions for faster, more complete recovery.
sports-performance-recovery.whatToExpect: Acute injuries typically respond within 3–6 sessions. Chronic overuse conditions may require a longer course of treatment. Many athletes incorporate regular sessions during competitive seasons for ongoing recovery support and injury prevention. Treatment plans are adjusted based on your training schedule, competition calendar, and how your body responds.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help me recover faster between training sessions?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture supports circulation, reduces inflammation, and helps regulate the nervous system — all of which directly influence how quickly your body recovers from training load. Many athletes notice improved recovery time and reduced soreness with regular treatment.

faqs.q: When should I get acupuncture before a race or event?
faqs.a: Pre-event treatment is typically best scheduled 2–5 days before your event — close enough to benefit from the effects, but with enough time for your body to integrate the treatment. Post-event sessions can be scheduled as soon as 24–48 hours after to support recovery.

faqs.q: Is acupuncture safe during a training season?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture is drug-free and non-disruptive to training. It can be scheduled alongside your regular workouts, and treatment plans are always adapted to your training calendar and competition schedule.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture prevent injuries?
faqs.a: Regular acupuncture helps identify and address movement compensations, muscular imbalances, and overuse patterns before they develop into injuries. Many athletes use it proactively as part of their overall training support rather than only reactively after something goes wrong.

faqs.q: What is motor point needling and how is it different from regular acupuncture?
faqs.a: Motor point needling targets the specific location where the motor nerve enters the muscle. Stimulating these points releases tension throughout the entire muscle and restores normal neuromuscular firing patterns — making it especially effective for athletic injuries, movement dysfunction, and overuse conditions.

facial-rejuvenation-cosmetic.title: Facial Rejuvenation & Cosmetic Acupuncture
facial-rejuvenation-cosmetic.tagline: Natural skin rejuvenation, facial muscle tone, and a glow that starts from within
overview: Facial rejuvenation acupuncture is a non-invasive treatment designed to support skin health, facial muscle tone, circulation, and overall facial vitality. Unlike injectable treatments, fillers, or more invasive procedures, cosmetic acupuncture works with your body's own regenerative capacity — with no downtime, no side effects, and results that reflect genuine health rather than surface-level correction.

At Five Points Wellness, treatments are customized to support natural collagen and elastin production, improved facial muscle tone and lift, and healthy circulation — while also addressing internal factors such as stress, sleep, hormonal balance, and digestion. The result is a glow that comes from within, not just from the surface.

introSections.title: How Cosmetic Acupuncture Works
paragraphs: Cosmetic acupuncture works by stimulating the body's natural physiological processes involved in skin health and tissue repair. Fine needles inserted into specific facial points create a controlled micro-stimulus that triggers collagen and elastin synthesis, improves local microcirculation, and relaxes the chronic muscular tension patterns that contribute to lines, wrinkles, and loss of contour.

Because the skin reflects both internal health and external stressors, treatment supports both facial aesthetics and whole-body regulation. Facial cupping and gua sha are often integrated to enhance lymphatic drainage, reduce puffiness, and further stimulate tissue renewal.

introSections.title: Facial Motor Points & Natural Lifting
paragraphs: A key component of advanced cosmetic acupuncture involves working with facial motor points — specific anatomical locations where motor nerves activate facial muscles. These points are used to support facial muscle function and encourage natural lifting effects by improving neuromuscular communication and circulation.

By targeting these motor points, treatment may help improve facial muscle tone and firmness, support natural lifting of facial structures, reduce areas of muscular stagnation or tension, and enhance definition along the jawline, cheeks, and brow. This approach works with the natural function of facial muscles to encourage healthier tone, structure, and movement over time.

addresses: Loss of facial tone and elasticity

sections.title: What Sets This Treatment Apart
paragraphs: Cosmetic acupuncture at Five Points Wellness integrates traditional acupuncture for systemic balance, facial motor point stimulation for lift and tone, circulation-focused techniques for skin health, and nervous system regulation for stress-related aging patterns — all in a single treatment.

Because facial appearance is closely linked to stress, sleep, digestion, and hormonal balance, treatment is designed to support both your aesthetic goals and your internal wellness simultaneously. This is what creates the "glow from within" quality that patients notice — not just a surface improvement, but a whole-system shift that shows up in the skin.

sections.title: Microneedling & Integrative Acupuncture Support
paragraphs: Microneedling is also offered as a separate aesthetic service focused on skin resurfacing and collagen stimulation. Both treatments can be incorporated into your overall treatment plan; however, they require separate appointments and cannot be performed on the same day, due to the nature of each modality and optimal skin recovery protocols.

During microneedling sessions, distal acupuncture points are offered as a complimentary component to support circulation and tissue healing, promote nervous system regulation and relaxation, and enhance the body's internal regenerative response. This integrative approach allows microneedling to work not only on the surface of the skin, but in coordination with the body's internal systems involved in repair and regeneration.

sections.title: Holistic Skin Health
paragraphs: Skin health is influenced by multiple internal factors including stress and cortisol levels, sleep quality, digestion and gut health, hormonal balance, hydration, and circulation. For this reason, treatment is designed to support not only facial appearance, but also the internal systems that influence skin aging and vitality.

Each session incorporates both facial and constitutional (whole-body) treatment, addressing the internal imbalances that show up in the skin. The result is an improvement in skin quality alongside broader wellness benefits — radiance, improved energy, and a sense of ease that patients frequently notice beyond the mirror.

facial-rejuvenation-cosmetic.howItHelps: Collagen and elastin production are stimulated through controlled needle micro-stimulus, improving skin structure and elasticity over time. Microcirculation is enhanced to deliver oxygen and nutrients to facial tissues. Facial motor point techniques retrain and tone muscles for natural lift. And because the nervous system is also being regulated throughout treatment, stress-related skin aging patterns — one of the most overlooked contributors to facial change — are addressed directly.
facial-rejuvenation-cosmetic.whatToExpect: Treatments are generally relaxing and restorative. Most patients describe sessions as calming, grounding, and deeply releasing — with an immediate sense of facial "lightness" or lift. Results are gradual and cumulative: a course of 12 weekly sessions is recommended to start, with many patients noticing visible changes in skin tone, texture, and lift beginning around sessions 6–8. Packages are available. Maintenance frequency is highly individual but typically falls in the range of every 4–6 weeks following the initial 12-session series, and continues to build as collagen activity and tissue tone improve over time.

faqs.q: Does cosmetic acupuncture have side effects?
faqs.a: Unlike injectable treatments, fillers, or surgical options, cosmetic acupuncture has no downtime and no significant side effects. Minor temporary redness or a small bruise at a needle site is possible but uncommon. Most patients leave looking and feeling noticeably better immediately after treatment.

faqs.q: How many sessions do I need?
faqs.a: A series of 12 weekly sessions is the recommended starting course. Many patients notice visible changes beginning around sessions 6–8. Packages are available to support you through the full initial series.

faqs.q: What does maintenance look like after the initial series?
faqs.a: Maintenance is highly individual and depends on your skin, lifestyle, and goals. Most patients transition to maintenance sessions every 4–6 weeks following the initial 12-session series. Your response to treatment will guide the recommendation.

faqs.q: Does facial acupuncture hurt?
faqs.a: No. Treatments use very fine needles and are generally well tolerated and deeply relaxing. Most patients are surprised by how comfortable — even pleasant — the experience is.

faqs.q: Can cosmetic acupuncture and microneedling be combined?
faqs.a: Both can be part of an integrated treatment plan but are always scheduled on separate days. Distal acupuncture points are included during microneedling sessions to support your body's healing response from the inside.

faqs.q: Does cosmetic acupuncture improve muscle tone?
faqs.a: Yes. Facial motor point techniques are a core component of treatment and are used specifically to support improved facial muscle tone, firmness, and natural lift over time.

pediatric-acupuncture.title: Pediatric Acupuncture
pediatric-acupuncture.tagline: Gentle, Non-Invasive Support for Children's Health & Development
overview: Pediatric acupuncture offers a gentle, individualized approach to supporting children's physical, emotional, and developmental health. Treatments are adapted specifically for children's sensitivity, comfort level, and age.

At Five Points Wellness, care is designed to be calming, safe, and often needle-free when appropriate. Many children benefit from techniques such as Shōnishin (Japanese pediatric acupuncture), acupressure, moxibustion, cupping, and pediatric Tuina (gentle therapeutic massage).
For children under 7, or those who are anxious, sensitive, or not comfortable with needles — needles will not be used. Non-needle approaches are used in these cases, full stop.

introSections.title: How Pediatric Acupuncture Works
paragraphs: Children are not simply "small adults." In Traditional Chinese Medicine, a child's system is considered more dynamic and responsive, with Qi (energy and physiological function) circulating more superficially than in adults. Because of this, treatments are typically very gentle and often require minimal stimulation.

Rather than strong or deep techniques, pediatric acupuncture uses light touch stimulation, non-needle Shōnishin methods, and shorter sessions focused on calming the nervous system and supporting natural regulation and development.

sections.title: Shōnishin — Non-Needle Pediatric Acupuncture
paragraphs: Shōnishin is a specialized Japanese pediatric technique that uses small, non-invasive tools to gently stimulate the skin and meridian pathways without needles. It is especially suited for young children and infants, first-time pediatric patients, and children with needle sensitivity, anxiety, or sensory processing differences.
Shōnishin is designed to regulate the nervous system, support digestion, improve sleep, and promote emotional balance — all without a single needle.

sections.title: Additional Pediatric Treatment Modalities
paragraphs: Depending on the child's needs, treatment may also incorporate moxibustion — a gentle warming therapy that supports circulation, digestion, and immune function — as well as very light pediatric cupping to support respiratory health and muscle relaxation.

Pediatric Tuina, a gentle form of Chinese medical massage, may also be used to support digestion, sleep, immunity, and emotional regulation, particularly for younger children or those who respond well to touch-based care.

sections.title: Parent & Child Family Support Sessions
paragraphs: For children experiencing stress, anxiety, or emotional dysregulation, treatment may include parent-and-child sessions focused on calming the nervous system and supporting emotional connection. These sessions combine gentle treatment for the child with education for parents on calming techniques and nervous system regulation strategies that can be carried into daily life.
This approach helps extend the benefits of treatment beyond the clinic and supports emotional transitions and behavioral patterns at home.

pediatric-acupuncture.howItHelps: Pediatric acupuncture regulates the nervous system, supports immune function, and addresses the underlying patterns that contribute to recurring health challenges in children. Treatment is always guided by the child's response and tolerance, and is fully adapted to age, comfort level, and individual needs.
pediatric-acupuncture.whatToExpect: Sessions are calm, gentle, and adapted to each child's comfort level. Most children experience treatment as calming and often report feeling relaxed or sleepy afterward. Sessions are typically shorter than adult treatments. Treatment plans are adjusted frequently as children respond and their needs evolve.

faqs.q: Does pediatric acupuncture use needles?
faqs.a: Not always. Many children are treated using Shōnishin (non-needle techniques), acupressure, moxibustion, cupping, or gentle massage. If a child is not comfortable with needles, they will not be used — period.

faqs.q: Is it safe for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Pediatric acupuncture techniques are gentle, non-invasive, and tailored specifically for children's physiology and comfort.

faqs.q: What ages can be treated?
faqs.a: Children of all ages can be seen, including infants, toddlers, school-age children, and adolescents.

faqs.q: Will my child be uncomfortable?
faqs.a: Most children find treatment relaxing. Techniques are adjusted based on comfort level, and if a child is not ready for or comfortable with needles, they will not be used at all.

surgical-recovery-scar-treatment.title: Surgical Recovery & Scar Treatment
surgical-recovery-scar-treatment.tagline: Supporting tissue healing, reducing pain, and restoring function after surgery
overview: Acupuncture can be used as a supportive therapy before and after surgery to help prepare the body for recovery and assist with the healing process.

In the weeks leading up to surgery, treatment is often focused on optimizing circulation, reducing stress, and supporting overall nervous system regulation. In many cases, 2 sessions per week for 2–4 weeks prior to surgery may be recommended when appropriate to help prepare the body for optimal recovery.
addresses: Nerve pain and numbness near surgical sites
Restricted range of motion and fascial restriction

sections.title: Post-Surgical Recovery Support
sections.description: Following surgery, acupuncture may be used as part of a post-operative recovery plan. Treatment frequency is adjusted based on surgical type, healing stage, and individual response.

sections.title: Scar Tissue & Fascial Restriction Treatment
sections.description: Once a surgical scar is fully healed and cleared by your medical provider, acupuncture can be used to support long-term tissue mobility and recovery. Scar tissue can sometimes contribute to local tightness or sensitivity, fascial restrictions, reduced range of motion, compensatory movement patterns, and discomfort or pulling sensations around the affected area.
paragraphs: A specialized acupuncture technique sometimes used in scar care is known as "Surround the Dragon." This method involves placing very fine, shallow needles in a circular or surrounding pattern around the scar or along segments of the scar tissue. The goal is to gently stimulate local circulation and support the release of fascial restrictions that may develop during healing.
This approach may be used to support improved tissue mobility, comfort, and functional movement patterns over time.

sections.title: Post-Anesthesia Urinary Retention
paragraphs: Following certain surgeries, residual anesthetic agents can temporarily affect the nerves that control bladder function, leading to urinary retention — an inability to fully empty the bladder. This is particularly observed after hip replacement surgery, where the proximity of the surgical site to the bladder and its surrounding nerve supply can be a contributing factor.

Acupuncture may be used to support the return of normal bladder function by stimulating specific points along the sacral and lower abdominal regions that are associated with bladder and urogenital regulation. By influencing the local nerve pathways and promoting nervous system regulation in the pelvic area, treatment is aimed at helping restore normal bladder signaling.
This is an area where acupuncture can serve as a timely and targeted supportive intervention during post-operative recovery, working alongside conventional medical management.

surgical-recovery-scar-treatment.howItHelps: Acupuncture addresses both the systemic and local aspects of surgical recovery — reducing inflammation, supporting circulation to healing tissue, and helping regulate the nervous system pathways that influence pain, sensation, and organ function. Treatment evolves over time from general systemic support to more localized scar and mobility-focused care.
surgical-recovery-scar-treatment.whatToExpect: Surgical recovery support is individualized based on the type of procedure and stage of healing. Patients often report improved sense of circulation and warmth in the area, reduced tightness or pulling sensations, gradual improvement in mobility, decreased discomfort during movement, and a greater sense of overall recovery support. Acupuncture is used as a complementary therapy and is intended to support, not replace, post-surgical medical care.

faqs.q: When can I start acupuncture after surgery?
faqs.a: General recovery support can often begin within the first week or two post-surgery. Scar-specific treatment typically begins once the incision is fully healed and cleared by your provider, usually around 6–8 weeks.

faqs.q: Can acupuncture help with urinary retention after surgery?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture is commonly used to stimulate specific points that support bladder nerve signaling, particularly when urinary retention follows surgery involving areas near the pelvis, such as hip replacement.

faqs.q: Can I do acupuncture before my surgery?
faqs.a: Yes. Pre-surgical acupuncture focused on circulation, stress reduction, and nervous system regulation may help prepare the body for optimal recovery.

faqs.q: Is acupuncture safe after surgery?
faqs.a: When timed appropriately and performed by a licensed practitioner, acupuncture is generally safe as a post-operative supportive therapy. Treatment is always coordinated with your healing timeline.
